newsitem.title: BELARUS: Ford boosting E. Europe profile via Belarus.
newsitem.headline: Ford boosting E. Europe profile via Belarus.

text.p: Ford Motor Co., the world's second-largest automaker, said Thursday it plans to boost its presence in Eastern Europe by opening a vehicle assembly plant near the Belarus capital Minsk.
"This investment will help us to be a major participant in the region," Wayne Booker, Ford vice chairman, said from his office at Ford headquarters in Dearborn, Mich.
"You will see a higher profile for Ford in Eastern Europe over the next several years -- there's no doubt about that," he added.

Ford is planning to invest only $9.8 million in Belarus for a 51 percent stake in a $19.2 million plant with an annual capacity to assemble 6,000 units of Escort cars and Transit vans from imported parts.
But Ford said the venture, named Ford Union (FU), was full of symbolism and potential. The plant will be located at Obchuck, four miles northeast of Minsk.

FU's opening ceremony July 30 will mark the first time that passenger vehicles will be built in Belarus, which became a major manufacturer of agricultural tractors and heavy trucks for the old East Bloc.
The Belarus Escorts also will be the first West European cars to be made since the end of communism in the former Soviet Union, where the only foreign brands in production are American and Korean.
The Belarus government took 26 percent of the venture by providing $4 million in facilities and land, $1 million in cash and a package of tax breaks, Ford said.
The remaining 23 percent is held by Lada-OMC, a Belarus-British venture that imports and services Ford vehicles.
